item.title: Pharma Headlines - Tuesday, September 15, 2026: GSK buys a second Chimagen trispecific T-cell engager for multiple myeloma in a deal worth up to $750M; FDA approves Curium's Bexlutry, the first-ever radioligand equivalent, via 505(b)(2) against Novartis's Lutathera; Sanofi hands Cheplapharm 20 mature medicines and three plants for a 26.4% equity stake; gotistobart nearly doubles OS over docetaxel in previously treated squamous NSCLC (18.5 vs 10.0 months); Sionna cuts 46% of staff and keeps only its dual CFTR corrector combo; Electra sets terms for a ~$325M Nasdaq IPO; FDA opens Operation TrialBlazer applications; and Definium posts a third positive Phase 3 for oral lysergide, this one in generalized anxiety
item.description: Your biotech and pharma briefing for Tuesday, September 15, 2026. With WCLC winding down, the flow rotates back to deals, regulatory firsts and capital markets. The lead, and today's spotlight: GSK acquired global rights to a preclinical trispecific T-cell engager from Chimagen Biosciences - CD3 plus two tumor-associated antigens on the myeloma cell - for an undisclosed upfront and milestones totaling up to $750M, with Phase 1 expected in 2027. It is GSK's second Chimagen asset after the October 2024 deal for CMG1A46 (CD19 x CD20 high-affinity, CD3 low-affinity; $300M upfront plus $550M in milestones), and the repeated architecture is the story. GSK is separately cutting 650 jobs closing a German vaccine plant. Also: the FDA approved Curium's BEXLUTRY (lutetium Lu 177 dotatate) for SSTR-positive GEP-NETs - the first radioligand equivalent ever cleared, under 505(b)(2) against Lutathera on published evidence plus bridging data, with Curium selling supply reliability off four sites and full lutetium vertical integration; Sanofi and Cheplapharm will transfer 20 mature medicines (Lovenox among them) and three plants in Hungary, Singapore and France, with Sanofi taking a 26.4% equity stake rather than cash, closing through Q3 2027; BioNTech and OncoC4's PRESERVE-003 stage 1 showed gotistobart - a CTLA-4 antibody engineered to deplete intratumoral Tregs - at 18.5 months median OS versus 10.0 for docetaxel in previously treated squamous NSCLC post-checkpoint; Sionna is cutting 46% of staff, dropping everything but its dual NBD1-corrector combination into a Phase 2a, with $268.3M and runway into 2028; Electra Therapeutics set IPO terms at 21.7M shares at $14-16 (~$325M at midpoint, just under $1B fully diluted) behind pan-SIRP antibody ipsoprubart in the registrational SURPASS trial in secondary HLH; the FDA opened applications for Operation TrialBlazer, an expedited IND pilot pairing 8-10 sponsors with qualified research institutions for rolling pre-IND review, targeting up to 12 months off the path to first-in-human, applications due October 30; and Definium's Panorama Phase 3 of DT120 ODT (lysergide) in GAD hit its primary endpoint - 100 microgram arm -9.8 on HAM-A versus -4.7 placebo, a 5.1-point placebo-adjusted difference, p<0.0001, Cohen's d 0.64, n=245 - on the same day the FDA held its public hearing on therapeutic psychedelics at White Oak. Week ahead: TrialBlazer applications October 30, psychedelics comments close October 5, Electra pricing this week, UX111 on the 19th, Winrevair label update on the 21st, zilurgisertib on the 26th, Caspian's menin data on the 29th.
item.itunes:summary: Tuesday, September 15, 2026. GSK bought a second trispecific T-cell engager from China's Chimagen Biosciences - CD3 plus two tumor antigens on the myeloma cell - for an undisclosed upfront and up to $750M in total value, Phase 1 in 2027; it also cut 650 jobs closing a German vaccine plant. The FDA approved Curium's BEXLUTRY, the first radioligand equivalent ever cleared, a 505(b)(2) against Novartis's Lutathera in SSTR-positive GEP-NETs, sold on supply reliability rather than new outcomes data. Sanofi is handing Cheplapharm 20 mature medicines including Lovenox plus three plants in exchange for a 26.4% equity stake. Out of Seoul, BioNTech and OncoC4's gotistobart - a Treg-depleting CTLA-4 antibody - posted 18.5 versus 10.0 months median OS against docetaxel in previously treated squamous NSCLC. Sionna is cutting 46% of staff and keeping only its dual NBD1-corrector combination. Electra Therapeutics set terms for a ~$325M Nasdaq IPO behind pan-SIRP antibody ipsoprubart in secondary HLH. The FDA opened Operation TrialBlazer applications, an expedited IND pilot aimed at reshoring early-phase trials, due October 30. And Definium's third positive Phase 3 for oral lysergide, this one in generalized anxiety, landed the same day as the FDA's psychedelics hearing.
